devdoc.author: Altitude Labs*
devdoc.details: Implementation of access restrictions for the vault functions

RoleAdminChanged(bytes32,bytes32,bytes32.details: Emitted when `newAdminRole` is set as ``role``'s admin role, replacing `previousAdminRole` `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` is the starting admin for all roles, despite {RoleAdminChanged} not being emitted signaling this. _Available since v3.1._

RoleGranted(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is granted `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call, an admin role bearer except when using {AccessControl-_setupRole}.

RoleRevoked(bytes32,address,address).details: Emitted when `account` is revoked `role`. `sender` is the account that originated the contract call:   - if using `revokeRole`, it is the admin role bearer   - if using `renounceRole`, it is the role bearer (i.e. `account`)

getRoleAdmin(bytes32).details: Returns the admin role that controls `role`. See {grantRole} and {revokeRole}. To change a role's admin, use {_setRoleAdmin}.

grantRole(bytes32,address).details: Grants `role` to `account`. If `account` had not been already granted `role`, emits a {RoleGranted} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleGranted} event.

renounceRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from the calling account. Roles are often managed via {grantRole} and {revokeRole}: this function's purpose is to provide a mechanism for accounts to lose their privileges if they are compromised (such as when a trusted device is misplaced). If the calling account had been revoked `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must be `account`. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

revokeRole(bytes32,address).details: Revokes `role` from `account`. If `account` had been granted `role`, emits a {RoleRevoked} event. Requirements: - the caller must have ``role``'s admin role. May emit a {RoleRevoked} event.

selectedFunctions.label: Altitude borrow wstETH collateral and USDC debt position
warnings: Static deployment/source/ABI metadata only; not live authorization, persistent runtime attestation, backing, liquidity, financial safety, successful execution or a complete workflow. Independent grants, policies, pauses and canonical calldata/value controls remain mandatory; zero native value required.

Ethereum public Live wstETH-USDC v2 vault only, exact root 0xaf6062222d00Ac63477aD084Ebd22a7821E5EE8d. Current root resolves VaultERC20 0x5481D5627Aa367aA677442a120Fd1021aB0595D5; current snapshot delegate manager observed 0x090056ffbe50ad88afa881e735bce9bd9c2e84d8, full applicable sources+ABIs retained. Sourcify root/implementation/manager runtime and creation grades are match (partial metadata match), NOT exact_match. Official docs label the product v2 while applicable code paths contain vaults/v1; this is recorded, not silently relabeled. Private paused-yield v1 is not admitted.

Collateral is configured wstETH in native 18-decimal units; borrowed/repaid/claimed asset is configured USDC in native 6-decimal units. Own interest-bearing supply/debt-token accounting plus lender/farm routing differs from a bare asset transfer. All selected calls update borrower position/interest and may commit harvest profits, supply losses or debt changes first. ERC20 VaultERC20 deposit/depositAndBorrow ABI is payable but does not consume msg.value; send ZERO native value to avoid trapping ETH.

deposit(amount,onBehalfOf) pulls collateral exclusively from msg.sender, routes to fixed active lender, and mints supply-account balance based on actual lender deposit to the named account. onBehalfOf must be caller or already allowed through the contract permission list/function validation; no grant is made. depositAndBorrow deposits and borrows for caller. No arbitrary target/calldata input or new delegation/borrow-signature methods admitted.

borrow(amount) incurs debt only for msg.sender and sends USDC only to caller; health-factor/ingress checks and vault-wide capacity apply. It may source funds from lender and/or configured farm, with debt-token redistribution. Collateral and debt depend on oracle prices, liquidation thresholds, interest, supply/farm loss, governance-mutable strategies and hooks. Self-repayment is not guaranteed.

repay(amount,onBehalfOf) pulls only payer USDC, caps repayment at recorded debt and burns corresponding debtor balance; other-account repayment requires already-existing contract permission, which catalog never grants. repayBadDebt pulls only payer USDC and requires debtor supply balance zero, intentionally bypassing on-behalf allowlist; it does not grant control over debtor funds. repayAndWithdraw repays caller debt then withdraws caller collateral to chosen recipient.

withdraw(amount,to) uses caller supply position, caps by caller balance and total actual lender supply, checks borrower/vault health, may withdraw farm USDC to repay vault debt, and sends actual lender-returned wstETH to recipient. Withdrawal fee reduces collateral; additional lender shortfall is reflected in actual output without a caller minimum-output bound. Source distributes early-withdrawal fee among remaining supply holders by interest index; rounding can reduce last exiting holder amount. No redemption queue or promised payout amount/date.

claimRewards(amountRequested) only claims caller earnings after accounting; existing debt and losses consume earnings first by moving covered debt to vault. Remaining requested payout is capped by available claimable earnings and actual farm return, and USDC goes only to caller. Zero requested amount may only reduce debt; no minimum payout/harvest guarantee. Harvest reserves and mutable distribution terms reduce rewards.

Point-in-time official ingress 0xc2E2F4CB58c4DcCF21A8aa47529B09c39C029e14 had pause=false and selected deposit/borrow/withdraw/repay/rewards/commit validators disabled=false; early withdrawal fee factor observed 5000000000000000/1e18 (0.5%) for 150 blocks. Limits, sanctions, rate limits, roles and function flags remain mutable and can prevent execution; observations are not continuing availability guarantees.

Owner config/upgrades, delegated manager endpoints, public snapshot/position maintenance, operator rebalance/loss snapshots, third-party liquidation, supply-token callbacks, authorization lists and borrowOnBehalfOf wallet signature authority are excluded. No whole-workflow, dependency runtime/safety, external lender/farm solvency or offchain service assurance.
